title: etbb-july-2024-may-2025-update.pdf — section 336
text:
112. Research suggests that women released from prison are twice as likely to reoffend as a
comparable cohort of women given community orders.312 Over 70% of women who have
served a sentence of less than 12 months have reoffended.313 The National Offender
Management Service (now HM Prison and Probation Service) says it supports the reduction
of the number of women sentenced to custodial sentences in appropriate cases by
developing robust community sentences tailored to the needs of the individual women.314

113. Alternatively, if a prison sentence is necessary, strong personal mitigation or a realistic
prospect of rehabilitation might suggest it is appropriate to suspend the sentence.315

114. There is also power to defer passing sentence for up to six months under the powers of the
Criminal Courts (Sentencing) Act 2000, eg to allow an offender to undergo addiction or
mental health treatment prior to sentencing.
